title: The Whole Sachet
logline: On her ninth wedding night a vanishing bride is caught doctoring the groom's milk. He is awake, he has padlocked the door, and he has spent fourteen months making himself her mark to reach the woman who sends the brides, and the bride who robbed his little brother. All he has of that bride is a photograph of her scarred left hand. The scar is on Kiran's arm, under her bangles.
language_note: en-IN: Indian English, same cast as the Hinglish cut. Names and Indian terms kept as spoken in India: Mausi, Bhaiya, beta, lakh.
script_note: Indian English in Latin script; Indian terms kept (Mausi, Bhaiya, beta, lakh). Not British, not American.

characters.name: Kiran
characters.role: LEAD. The bureau's vanishing bride, on her ninth wedding night. Tonight she is 'Sneha' to the groom.
characters.look: Indian woman, 27, about 5 ft 3, slight and wiry. Wheat-brown skin, oval face, straight dark brows, large kajal-lined eyes, closed watchful mouth. Low bun, centre parting with a thin line of sindoor, two loose strands at the temples, small round red bindi, thin plain gold ring in the LEFT nostril, small gold studs, short black-bead mangalsutra. Plain sindoor-red matte silk-cotton saree with a 1 cm plain gold border, red elbow-length blouse, pallu over the left shoulder; drawn over her head only in her first moments as 'Sneha'. Barefoot. Block henna: a solid disc in each palm and every fingertip dipped to the first joint, backs of the hands plain. On each forearm a red-and-ivory chooda that reads as one red cuff about 10 cm long with a pale band at each end. Tonight both cuffs are pushed up toward the elbows so they cannot clink. Her LEFT forearm is never seen uncovered until b11 (production lock).
characters.voice_note: Same voice as the Hinglish cut. Female, late 20s, alto with a dry edge. Small-city Madhya Pradesh Indian English, learnt at school and from a phone: simple, quick, contractions, a light Hindi accent, no British or American colour. Two registers, one actor. 'Sneha' (l02, l06): half a tone higher, soft, polite and tentative, sentences that trail off. Kiran (from l11): lower, flat, quick, blunt, short sentences. Under pressure she gets quieter and more exact, never shrill.

characters.name: Aditya
characters.role: The groom. A pharmacist who has made himself the bureau's mark to find the woman who sends the brides, and the bride who robbed his brother Mohit.
characters.look: Indian man, 33, about 6 ft, tall and narrow with a slight stoop. Light-brown skin, long clean-shaven face, high forehead, calm deep-set eyes, thin mouth, short neat black hair with a left side parting. Rimless rectangular glasses in every shot, including with his eyes shut. Plain cream cotton-silk wedding kurta with a band collar and three cloth buttons, sleeves folded back once, a side pocket on the right; cream churidar; barefoot. A brass key about 5 cm long on a doubled red cotton thread, outside the kurta at mid-chest, in every shot. Plain steel watch on a brown strap on the left wrist, never readable.
characters.voice_note: Same voice as the Hinglish cut. Male, early 30s, light baritone, soft-spoken. Careful small-city Madhya Pradesh Indian English, a science graduate's: complete sentences, precise nouns (sedative, SIM, proof, police, bureau, photo, reception), no slang, a clear Indian accent, no British or American colour. Even and unhurried, almost courteous, like a man reading out a prescription. Never shouts. Under pressure he slows down and drops in volume; the one place the voice may catch is his brother's name.

characters.name: Billu
characters.role: The bride's 'brother', driver and lookout. Waiting in the car in the lane.
characters.look: Indian man, 30, about 5 ft 7, wiry and restless. Brown skin, sharp jaw, patchy stubble, black hair gelled straight back. Faded blue denim jacket with the sleeves pushed up over a black round-neck T-shirt, dark jeans. A wooden toothpick in the right corner of his mouth; a car key on a plain steel ring hooked on his right index finger. No weapon.
characters.voice_note: Same voice as the Hinglish cut. Male, about 30, light tenor, fast, a little nasal, talks round a toothpick. Quick small-town Bundelkhand Indian English with a strong Hindi accent, an article dropped now and then; never American street slang. To Mausi: quick and obedient.

characters.name: Shakun Mausi
characters.role: Runs the bureau and the brides. Voice on Billu's phone only; never seen in this episode.
characters.look: Not seen in s1e01. Voice only.
characters.voice_note: Same voice as the Hinglish cut. Female, mid 50s, low, warm and grainy, a paan-chewer's unhurried mouth. Warm, motherly Indian English in short plain sentences with a heavy Bundelkhand Hindi accent; Hindi endearments kept (beta) and English ones in the same spirit ('my poor girl'). She sounds like someone's aunt at a wedding. Laughs easily; never raises her voice. On the phone she is fully voiced and clear, never a whisper. Light phone filter in the mix.

characters.name: Mohit
characters.role: Aditya's dead younger brother. Only a hand in the photograph; no voice. His death is never pictured.
characters.look: Only in the photograph (b9): a young man's right hand, palm up, light-brown skin, a red thread at the wrist, the cuff of a cream kurta. Never a face.

location: The bridal bedroom of a rented house (first floor, about 3 by 3.5 m): double bed with a dark wood headboard against the back wall, white sheet, one red bolster, loose marigold petals, marigold strings in a fringe above the headboard; lime-washed pale-green walls, one bare nail, no pictures. From the foot of the bed facing it: the window with an iron grille and open shutters in the RIGHT wall, the grey-green steel almirah against the LEFT wall with a wooden chair holding Kiran's maroon bag, the pale-blue double door BEHIND, bolted and padlocked on the inside. A low stool on the window side of the bed holds a steel tray with the steel glass and the paper fold. One warm amber bedside lamp on the almirah side (key), cool blue-white streetlight through the grille (rim), no overhead light. Cutaway: the empty lane below, Billu's old white sedan under one sodium streetlight, shutters down, no readable signs.
time_of_day: Night 1, late April, about 1:35 to 1:45 am. Warm night, window open.

beats.action: HOOK, the image lands at 0 s. Set-up 1 (from the start of l01): extreme close-up of Kiran's RIGHT hand, fingertips dipped in henna, tapping white powder from a small folded paper पुड़िया into a steel glass of pale-yellow kesar milk on the steel tray on the stool by the window. Her right chooda is pushed up toward the elbow, out of frame or at its edge; the red pallu at frame edge. Her left arm is not in frame: it is under the fall of the pallu (production lock, b1 to b10). Warm lamp key, cool streetlight rim. l01 is Aditya off screen, lying dressed on the bed with his eyes shut. Set-up 2 (from 'आधी में'): the same framing, the hand stopped in the air, half the powder still in the fold.

lines.speaker: aditya
lines.text: [calm] Pour in the whole sachet. Half doesn't put me to sleep.

beats.action: Set-up 1 (l02, first sentence): Aditya sitting up on the marigold-strewn bed, unhurried, rimless glasses already on, the brass key on its red thread against the cream kurta, the red bolster behind him, her black phone in its dark-red cover face up on the sheet beside him. Set-up 2 (l02, second sentence): Kiran turned from the stool toward him as 'Sneha': pallu drawn over her head, eyes lowered, right hand at her chest, the fold left on the tray behind her; left arm under the pallu. Set-up 3 (l03 to 'स्नेहा'): Aditya MCU, hands in his lap, calm. Insert (l03 from 'इसीलिए केसर'): the steel glass on the tray, untouched, a few saffron strands on the milk. He does not touch the glass.

lines.speaker: kiran
lines.text: [nervous] You're awake? I was only putting saffron in your milk.

lines.speaker: aditya
lines.text: [calm] A sedative is bitter, Sneha. That's why the saffron, isn't it?

beats.action: Set-up 1 (silent): Kiran at the pale-blue double door, back to camera, her RIGHT hand on the iron bolt; her left arm held against her body under the pallu. Insert (l04, first sentence): the iron bolt and hasp on the inside of the door, shut with a brass padlock. Insert (l04, second sentence): the brass key on its doubled red thread against his cream kurta, two of his fingers lifting it a little off the cloth. They stay a room's width apart: she at the door, he on the bed.

lines.speaker: aditya
lines.text: [quietly] I put the padlock on. The key is here.

beats.action: He takes the room apart, one insert per fact. Set-up 1 (l05, first sentence): Aditya at the open grey-green steel almirah, a red velvet box open in his hand: a necklace set that reads as gold, one scratched link showing dull brass. Set-up 2 (l05, second and third sentences): the bare lime-washed wall above the almirah, one bare nail, nothing else. Insert (l06): Kiran's black phone in its dark-red cover lying screen up on the white sheet among marigold petals; screen overlay 'No network' (overlay, not in the image). Kiran stays at the door; she does not pick it up. Insert (l07): a SIM card held up between his index and middle finger, his glasses and the key soft behind it.

lines.speaker: aditya
lines.text: [calm] The set is brass. The house is rented by the month. There's nothing here to steal.

lines.speaker: kiran
lines.text: [nervous] Can I just call my brother once? Bhaiya will worry.

lines.speaker: aditya
lines.text: [quietly] I have your SIM.

beats.action: Cut out to the lane. Set-up 1 (silent, then l08): the empty lane of shuttered houses; Billu's old white sedan under the single sodium streetlight; above it the warm square of the first-floor window behind its iron grille. Time overlay '1:40'. Set-up 2 (l09, with super su2): Billu in the driver's seat seen through the open side window, toothpick in the right corner of his mouth, car key hooked on his right index finger, phone at his ear, eyes turned up to the window. Set-up 3 (l27, then l10): low angle from beside the car up to the lit window, a marigold string dark against the grille. Mausi is a voice on his phone, heard for the first time; she is never seen. Nobody else in the lane.

lines.speaker: billu
lines.text: Yes, Mausi. I'm in the car below. Light is still on.

lines.speaker: mausi
lines.text: [chuckles] I'll phone the bride at two. Car at three, Billu.

lines.speaker: mausi
lines.text: [calm] Tonight she's playing Sneha, but she's still my Kiran.

lines.speaker: mausi
lines.text: [sighs] And listen, my poor girl must be hungry. Bring her straight to me.

beats.action: Back in the bedroom. Set-up 1 (l11): Kiran CU at the door; with her right hand she has pushed the pallu back off her head and 'Sneha' is gone from her face. The fall of the pallu still covers her left arm. Set-up 2 (l12, then l28): Aditya MCU, back on the edge of the bed. Set-up 3 (l13): Aditya, tighter, the key on its thread in frame. Set-up 4 (l14): two-shot across the room's width, Kiran at the door and Aditya on the bed, the stool with the tray and glass between them. Set-up 5 (l15): Kiran MCU, chin up, bargaining. Insert (l16): the brass padlock on the hasp again. Set-up 6 (l17): Aditya CU. Set-up 7 (l18): Kiran CU, Aditya's voice over it; she hears that the target is Mausi. Set-up 8 (l19): Kiran MCU, chin level, her right hand flat on the door; she asks. Her left arm stays under the pallu.

lines.speaker: kiran
lines.text: [cold] Fine. The act's over. Are you police?

lines.speaker: aditya
lines.text: [calm] Pharmacist. Honestly.

lines.speaker: aditya
lines.text: [quietly] My real name is Aditya. Your marriage bureau has a fake one.

lines.speaker: aditya
lines.text: [calm] Bureau, Bhaiya in the car, Mausi on the phone, bride gone by morning.

lines.speaker: aditya
lines.text: [quietly] It took me fourteen months to become your 'party'. The groom you rob.

lines.speaker: kiran
lines.text: [calm] This is my last wedding. Mausi has eighteen lakh of mine.

lines.speaker: kiran
lines.text: [quietly] I'll get you all of it. Just open the padlock.

lines.speaker: aditya
lines.text: [calm] I don't want money. The police told me to bring proof.

lines.speaker: aditya
lines.text: [quietly] For that proof, I need the woman who sends these brides.

lines.speaker: kiran
lines.text: [cold] What did Mausi ever do to you?

beats.action: Set-up 1 (l20): Aditya CU, eyes down at his hands, for the first time not looking at her. Set-up 2 (l21): Kiran CU: the name Mohit has landed; she does not move. Set-up 3 (l22): Aditya MCU, the breath going out of him. Insert (l23): his right hand drawing a creased 4x6 print from the side pocket of the kurta, its white back to camera.

lines.speaker: aditya
lines.text: [hesitant] My little brother, Mohit. Mausi arranged his wedding.

lines.speaker: aditya
lines.text: [quietly] I didn't go to the wedding. I was at the shop.

lines.speaker: aditya
lines.text: [sighs] There was no reception. The bride vanished with everything.

lines.speaker: aditya
lines.text: [calm] The bureau never sent her photo. She took Mohit's phone.

beats.action: Set-up 1 (l24): Aditya holds the creased print up toward her at arm's length, picture side to her, its white back to us; glasses and key in frame. Insert (l29, then silent): the photograph full frame, the one approved image used every time (story_locks.photograph): two hands on a stone temple step. A young man's right hand palm up, a red thread at the wrist, the cuff of a cream kurta. Laid on it, back of the hand to camera, a bride's LEFT hand with a new plain gold ring and no henna at all; about a dozen thin red glass bangles slid down to her wrist; above them on the outer forearm a pale crescent burn scar; the edge of a red veil at the top of the frame. No face, no chooda, no readable text.

lines.speaker: aditya
lines.text: [quietly] Only this survived. Mohit sent it from the temple.

lines.speaker: aditya
lines.text: [calm] The bride has a burn on her wrist, like a half moon.

beats.action: Set-up 1 (l25): Aditya MCU, the print lowered to his chest beside the key; said flat. Set-up 2 (silent, after the line): hold on Kiran's face, CU: she did not know. No tear, no movement; her right hand still against the door. The death is never pictured.

lines.speaker: aditya
lines.text: [flatly] Eleven days later, they found Mohit hanging from the fan.

beats.action: Set-up 1 (l26): Aditya CU, the print raised again beside his face; his eyes are on her face, not her hands. Set-up 2 (silent, about 2.5 s): low and close, behind the fall of her pallu and out of his line of sight, framed to mirror the b9 photograph: her LEFT forearm, back of the forearm to camera, crossing the frame at the same angle as the bride's forearm in the print; the red-and-ivory cuff still pushed up toward the elbow from the tray, and below it on the outer forearm, about three fingers above the wrist bone, the same pale crescent in the lamplight, at the same position and scale in frame as in the photograph. Set-up 3 (silent, about 1.5 s): the same framing, one change: her right hand has slid the cuff down and the crescent is gone under the red. Cut to black.

lines.speaker: aditya
lines.text: [quietly] I want this hand.

sfx_notes: Bedroom bed, b1 to b4 and b6 to b11, loopable: a warm April night through the open window, crickets, one far dog, a truck on a distant highway. Close, dry room tone. No ceiling fan anywhere in the episode (Mohit).
b1: paper tapped on the steel rim, a faint hiss of powder into milk. Aditya's l01 is off screen but close and dry, not distant: he is two metres away. Every sound stops with her hand on 'आधी में'.
b2: the bed creaks and marigold petals rustle as he sits up.
b3: bare feet on the floor; the iron bolt rattles against the hasp; the brass padlock knocks once on the iron and holds.
b4: the steel almirah door creaks; the velvet box hinge. The phone makes no sound.

b5: lane exterior: sodium-lamp hum, crickets, the toothpick clicking on Billu's teeth. Mausi through a light phone filter, fully voiced and warm, wide enough that consonants survive. Duck the lane bed under l27 so the names 'स्नेहा' and 'किरण' are both clear (the duck moves from l10 to l27 in the clarity pass).
b6 to b8: room tone only. Nothing under l13.
b8, l23: paper drawn from cloth; the print's crease.
b9, l29: room tone only under the photograph insert, so the line is fully clear.
b10: the crickets drop out under l25 and stay out through Kiran's hold.
b11: bed and music duck right down under l26 so it is fully clear. Last sound: one faint dry click of the chooda's bangles as the cuff slides down, close and small, then black and silence.
music_note: No music for b1 to b4: breath, paper and the padlock. A single low drone enters on the lane cut (b5) at the edge of hearing and carries under b6 and b8, never above the dialogue. It drops out entirely under l25. A low sustained note swells on the scar insert in b11 and cuts dead with the picture, leaving the bangle click alone.
ending_question: The hand Aditya has hunted for fourteen months is in the same room, under her chooda: when will he see that wrist, and what will he do when he does?

fixes.fault: Orchestrator read item 1: 'Nobody has told us this is a wedding night, she is the bride.' The English super 'Wedding night · 1:35 am' gives both roles by the end of b2 (ledger s1e01.f01).
cv_A s1e01 (2), cv_B: 'The set is brass. The house is rented by the month.' had to be worked out. Adds 'There's nothing here to steal.' (ledger default), so the premise is spoken by the end of b4.

Orchestrator item 5 and cv_A s1e01 (3): 'Who is Bhaiya?' English-only gloss in the same line: 'Can I just call my brother once? Bhaiya will worry.' (ledger default). Hindi needs none: भैया is the word.

Orchestrator item 6: new place, nobody placed. 'I'm in the car below' says where we are and ties the car to 'Bhaiya in the car' in l13. Billu's dropped article ('Light is still on') is kept for register.

cv_A s1e01 (3): 'Billu is never named here.' Mausi names him ('Car at three, Billu'), and 'beta' is dropped so the first 'beta' on the s1e02 call is for Kiran (ledger name_clashes). Super 'Billu · Mausi's driver' on set-up 2.
Orchestrator item 7: 'I'll phone her at two' had no clear 'her'. Now 'I'll phone the bride at two', mirroring 'दुल्हन को'.

cv_A s1e01 (1), cv_B 'Who is who': nothing links Sneha to Kiran. l27 'Tonight she's playing Sneha, but she's still my Kiran.' bridges the alias once, out of Aditya's hearing (lock). 'Playing' makes Sneha a role, not a second woman. The name leaves l10, which keeps Mausi's fretting as 'my poor girl must be hungry' (balance lever).
Orchestrator item 9: 'Jumps from pleading to cold with no turn.' 'The act's over.' mirrors 'नाटक ख़त्म'.

cv_A s1e01 (6): Aditya is never named. 'My real name is Aditya. Your marriage bureau has a fake one.' names him, glosses 'bureau' before the protected l13 (cv_A s1e01 (3)) and sets up s1b01 'Your name is fake'.
cv_A s1e01 (4), cv_B: 'In English, party means a celebration.' Glossed in the same line: 'your 'party'. The groom you rob.' The quotes mark the trade word in the subtitle.
cv_B s1e01: 'Take it all.' Take what? The money is with Mausi. Now 'I'll get you all of it.', which she can offer.

cv_B s1e01: 'He wants two different people within one minute.' l17 'The police told me to bring proof.' puts back the because; l18 'For that proof, I need the woman who sends these brides.' is the so. English uses 'need' for this instrumental aim so that 'want' stays with the personal one in the locked l26 ('I want this hand').

Orchestrator item 13, cv_B: Mohit's story was fragments. Now: no reception, the bride vanished with everything (l22); the bureau never sent her photo, she took Mohit's phone (l23); only this print survived, and Mohit sent it from the temple (l24). 'He' in l24 became 'Mohit' so the sender is not read as the bride.

cv_A s1e01 (5), cv_B: the photograph's burn is never said. 'The bride has a burn on her wrist, like a half moon.' (ledger default) says what the picture shows, never whose. It plays over the photograph insert, as in the Hindi.
